Piste reference data — confirm at source. Base = Alpe d'Huez village about 1,860 m (reference); summit 3,330 m (Pic Blanc) per search summary of the official ski-pass site. Vertical is village to summit; the satellite villages (Oz-en-Oisans, Vaujany and others) sit several hundred metres lower — confirm the lowest lift altitude

Figures describe the Alpe d'Huez Grand Domaine (5 villages). Search summary of the official ski-pass site: 250 km of slopes, 111 runs, 67 lifts, top 3,330 m. Lift types, hourly capacity and the colour split were not found; skiresort.info describes mainly gondolas and chairlifts, with a few drag lifts as practice lifts in the valleys.

Piste reference data — confirm at source. Only features Piste is confident about are set; everything else is unknown (null), not 'not offered'. Ski schools (e.g. ESF) and rental shops operate in the resort villages

character: Alpe d'Huez is a sunny resort in the Oisans, linked with Auris-en-Oisans, Villard-Reculas, Oz-en-Oisans and Vaujany in a domain of about 250 km and 111 runs up to Pic Blanc (3,330 m). It is known for long descents from the Pic Blanc glacier, such as the Sarenne black run (reference).
learning: Reference: the village has beginner areas and many easy runs close to the accommodation; confirm beginner-lift access and lessons for 2026-27.

announcedOpening.text: Alpe d'Huez opens 5 Dec 2026 (France Montagnes 2026-27 opening list, per search summary).
